title: Choose Appropriate Measures
objective: I can choose the best measure of center for a data set based on its shape.
model: dot plot and box plot of a data set where the mean is the balance point and an outlier pulls it while the median stays put

widgets.component: absolute deviation and MAD warm-up
widgets.root: Checked: 1.1-1.4 recompute (|26−20|=6, |11−15|=4, MAD 15÷5=3, lower MAD = more consistent); MAD is taught in 2-9 and is half of the 'mean and MAD' pair this lesson chooses between.

widgets.component: choose mean or median for a listed data set
widgets.root: Checked: gymnast 8.5-8.9 (mean 8.7), mile times with 12:00 (median 7:15), 5,6,7,7,8,50 (mean 13.83, median 7); each list is printed, the outlier is a number the student must notice, and each wrong choice names its misconception.

widgets.where: Practice §2 item 2.3 (sort, 4 data lists to Mean/Median)
widgets.component: sort real data lists by best measure
widgets.root: Checked: lists with and without an outlier (88-92 vs $250K, 1,2,1,0,2,1,15); the student must read the numbers, not a rule word.

widgets.where: Practice §2 item 2.5 and §3 item 3.3 (sort of rule phrases)
widgets.component: two near-duplicate sorts of phrases like 'No outliers' / 'Data is skewed' to Mean or Median
widgets.root: Both are the same six rule phrases sorted into the same two bins (2.5 has six cards, 3.3 repeats four of them); no data is shown, so the student recites a rule instead of seeing an outlier move the mean, while the lesson's manipulable (dotbalance) appears only once in Practice.
widgets.replacement: Delete 3.3. Replace 2.5 with act:dotbalance {goal:'outlier'} L1 (6 dots, mean triangle and median diamond live): 'Drag ONE dot so the mean equals the median.' Follow-up one-tap: 'Which measure moved more when you dragged the far dot?' (mean). Trap: choosing the median because 'it always stays put' (it does move if the dragged dot crosses the middle). Add a second dotbalance L2 in §3 in the slot of 3.3 with a low outlier.

widgets.component: spot the first wrong step: median of unordered data; mean chosen despite an outlier
widgets.root: Checked: 9,12,8,11,10 sorted gives median 10 not 8; 12,14,13,15,11,60 gives mean 20.8 and median 13.5; the flagged step is the first wrong one in both.

widgets.component: batting averages with an injury-shortened .110 season
widgets.root: Checked: mean .260 vs median .2875, outlier on the low side, distractors named.

widgets.where: Practice §3 item 3.2 (tbl, 2 data sets x Mean/Median/Outlier?/Best Measure)
widgets.component: fill-in table with free-text cells
widgets.root: The 'Outlier?' and 'Best Measure' cells are typed text graded by exact string (assets/studio/kinds-basic.js K.tbl): the key is 'Mean (no outlier, data is clustered)' and 'Median (72 pulls the mean to 27.6, higher than 4 of 5 values)', so a correct 'Median' is marked wrong and no student can match the sentence. The numeric cells (16.2, 16, 27.6, 17) are fine.
widgets.replacement: Keep the Mean and Median columns as typed numbers. Replace 'Outlier?' with a Yes/No tap and 'Best Measure' with a Mean/Median tap (k:'tbl' cell type 'pick', options ['Yes','No'] and ['Mean','Median'], graded by option index, not text). Keep both rows (15,18,16,17,15 and 15,18,16,17,72); after both are right show the sentence '72 pulls the mean to 27.6, above 4 of the 5 values' as the explanation.

widgets.component: generated outlier / effect-of-an-outlier / center-and-spread choices
widgets.root: Sampled seeds plus a 300-seed ambiguity scan of L3 (balanced data gets Mean and MAD, one outlier gets Median and IQR, 'Mode and range' is only a distractor) and L2 (adding 100 raises the mean a lot, median little). L1 'which value is the outlier' is thin but is a sound entry step.

widgets.component: draggable dot plot with live mean/median
widgets.root: The lesson's model: student drags dots and sees the mean move toward an outlier while the median hardly moves; the condition 'mean equals median, one dot moved' grades conditions, not a fixed answer.

widgets.component: mastery items whose scenario was dropped
widgets.root: The stems are 'What is the mean ticket price?', 'What is the median ticket price?' and 'Which measure better describes a typical ticket?' with no prices anywhere on the page: the six prices ($45, $50, $48, $52, $55, $260) live only in the config scenario and in the explanation shown after answering, so the items cannot be answered.
widgets.replacement: Put the data in each stem and add a figure: 'A reporter says the average playoff ticket costs $85. The six ticket prices are $45, $50, $48, $52, $55 and $260. What is the mean ticket price?' with viz {t:'dots', data:[45,48,50,52,55,260], min:40, max:270, step:20, label:'Ticket price ($)'}; repeat the sentence of prices in 5.2 and 5.3. Keys unchanged (85, 51, median).

widgets.component: choose a measure from a list; mean>median means right skew; median of 8 times
widgets.root: Checked: 15,18,16,17,15,72 (mean 25.5, median 16.5); mean 27 > median 21 gives skew right; 8 swim times sort to median (60.6+61.0)÷2=60.8 with named wrong answers.

widgets.component: effect of an added value; center and spread pair
widgets.root: Same generator as Practice; the 300-seed ambiguity scan found no repeated key value at L2-L3.

widgets.component: 'which summary best describes a typical value' with Mean/Median/Mode/Range choices
widgets.root: In 86 of 300 seeds a wrong choice carries the same number as the key (e.g. 90,72,93,112,80,97,455,105,93 offers 'Median, 93' and 'Mode, 93'), so two choices are defensible and the student who picks Mode is told they are wrong.
widgets.replacement: In assets/studio-gen/stats.js chooseMeasure L4, build the four choices so no wrong choice repeats the key's number: when the mode equals the median replace 'Mode, m' with 'Mean, x' or 'Middle of the range, r'; add an assertion that the four choice numbers are distinct to tools/studio-gen.test.mjs.

widgets.component: spot the first wrong step (mean despite outlier, unordered median, deleting a real outlier)
widgets.root: Checked sums and keys: 32,34,30,35,33,5 (mean 28.2, median 32.5); saves total 76 (10.9); serve speeds sort to median 104, not 107; deleting the recorded 31 is the first wrong step.

widgets.component: written explanation with a self-check rubric
widgets.root: The writing tasks require choosing a measure and justifying it with the outlier; rubric lines are lesson-specific.

widgets.component: four situations sorted by 'mean or median commonly reported'
widgets.root: Four cards (average temperature, class test score, median household income, median home price) are answered by naming the word in the card; no data shape is read, so it tests news-reporting trivia not the lesson's idea of choosing by shape.
widgets.replacement: Replace with a sort of four parametric dot plots (dots viz): symmetric, right-skewed, left-skewed, symmetric with one outlier; bins Mean and MAD / Median and IQR; each card shows the plot and the student decides from the shape.

widgets.where: Challenge §2 items 2.4, 2.5, 2.7, 4.4 and §5 items 5.1, 5.2, 5.5 (mc/num with dot plots)
widgets.component: dot plots with an outlier
widgets.root: Recomputed from the plotted data: rides mean 26, median 21; rebounds mean 8.5, median 6, IQR 2.5, MAD 4.625; bottles mean 25; recovery median 15, range 34, IQR 3.5; push-ups mean 16, median 19; attendance IQR 5.5; laps mean 61.7. Axes run min to max with even steps.

widgets.component: mean, median and gap for 32,35,36,38,39 vs 32,35,36,38,79
widgets.root: Numeric cells only (36, 36, 0, 44, 36, 8), all correct.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 items 3.1-3.2 (act:dotbalance outlier L3, spread L4)
widgets.component: draggable dot plot with mean, median and MAD readouts
widgets.root: Manipulable model; L4 'spread' keeps the mean fixed and changes MAD, which is the 'mean and MAD' half of the choice.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 item 3.3 and §5 item 5.3 (sort of six data lists; box plots)
widgets.component: pick the pair of measures from the data
widgets.root: Checked: symmetric sets map to Mean and MAD, skewed or outlier sets to Median and IQR; box plots Hawks IQR 0.8, Rams 1.6 with equal median 12.2.

widgets.component: effect of changing 40 to 400
widgets.root: 10,12,13,15,40 vs 10,12,13,15,400: median stays 13, mean 18 to 90; key 'only the mean changes'.
